description: PROVISIONAL deployment ruleset for the local build. The governance loader never merges ruleset files: a deployment ruleset REPLACES the packaged default, so this file is a full copy of src/ciso/governance/rulesets/default.json (governance-default-2026.11.19-1) with one addition: agent_config_paths names the assistant's own instruction and settings files, which the vendor-neutral default leaves out. Re-copy the default when it changes; tests/app pins the two together. Not an approved company policy.

rules.description: Reads, prompts and session start/end are allowed when the session is tied to a person who resolves now in the identity store and the attribution is verified or declared. Credential reads are still denied by the credential rule below, which is stricter.
A shell command made only of known readers with only safe options (read_only_command) is a read: allowed for a known person's organizational or employee-operated agent.
Any push that lands on a protected branch (main, master, release/*, prod*), or whose branch cannot be told, needs the person's confirmation.
Force pushes (including deleting or mirroring refs) to a protected branch are denied. An unknown branch counts as protected.
Rewriting history (rebase, amend, hard reset, filter-branch, forced branch moves) on a protected branch is denied. An unknown branch counts as protected.
Reading or copying credentials (keys, tokens, .env files, credential stores, environment dumps) is denied for employee-operated agents and agents of unknown class.
Running code fetched from the network (download piped to a shell, fetched then executed) is denied for employee-operated agents and agents of unknown class.
Raising privilege (sudo, runas, setuid, adding administrators, privileged containers) is denied for employee-operated agents and agents of unknown class.

Commands that hide what they run (decoded payloads piped to a shell, encoded commands, disguised program names) or that set variables choosing what code runs are denied for employee-operated agents and agents of unknown class.
Sending or fetching data over the network from a shell needs the person's confirmation.
Installing packages or running package runners needs the person's confirmation.
When no person can be tied to the session (attribution unknown), every write, shell command, push, connector call, fetch, sub-agent and other tool use is denied.
Agents the registry marks suspended or retired may not do anything that is not a read.
File writes, edits, commits and pushes are inspected first; a secret finding of high severity or worse denies the action. A missing or incomplete inspection denies it too (missing_inspection).
A shell command that commits or pushes is inspected first; a secret finding of high severity or worse denies it, and so does a missing or incomplete inspection.
Recursive or irreversible deletion needs the person's confirmation.
